clue.text: Grandfather taking sides — that hurts, one complains

indicators.note: the sides of the word Grandfather are its outermost letters, so only those two are used

parts.note: OUCH is what you cry when something hurts

explanation.surface: An elderly relative winces at a pain and starts grumbling about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking sides' keeps just the two ends of 'Grandfather', G and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A grouch is a habitual grumbler, someone who keeps finding fault.

clue.text: Gander caught in golf course

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed within the course word

parts.note: a lane is a course or track, as in a running lane
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A male goose gets trapped on a golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gander' looks like the bird, but here it is the informal noun for a look.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a gander is slang for having a quick look, which is a glance.

clue.text: Possibly 50 musicians or 100 — that guy's creative work is revolutionary

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
that guy's is a contraction of he is, written HE'S

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns round, so the word for creative work is read backwards

parts.note: art is creative work

explanation.surface: A boast about a man's groundbreaking art and the size of the ensemble involved.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in HE'S is ignored. 'Possibly' flags 50 as just an example size of the group.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large group of musicians, often around fifty to a hundred players.

clue.text: This poser is after snappy conversation

indicators.note: is after places the poser word behind the conversation words

parts.note: a snappy, irritable exchange is cross words
a poser is a puzzle or tricky question

explanation.surface: Someone striking a pose is chasing witty banter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' refers to the very thing the solver is doing. 'poser' looks like a person posing, but it means a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue's own self-reference: the item the solver is holding is a crossword puzzle.

clue.text: Projected suffering after boozing in different places

indicators.note: the two parts of the phrase swap places, so the first part moves to the end

parts.note: someone suffering after a drinking session is hung over

explanation.surface: Someone nursing a hangover after a session in a variety of bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in different places' tells you to swap HUNG and OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Overhung means jutting out above something, so it describes a part that projected.

clue.text: Swerve stag maybe when do's start is changed to five

indicators.note: is changed to swaps one letter of the animal word for the numeral

parts.note: a stag is an example of a deer

indicators.note: start asks for only the opening letter of the word do's

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A deer on a stag do swerves once the party gets going and five more turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stag' suggests a stag party alongside 'do', but here it is just a deer.
explanation.definitionFit: To veer is to change direction suddenly, which is what a swerve does.

clue.text: Drinks held up, bowed to both sides

parts.note: a round is a set of drinks bought for a group
to shoulder something is to bear or hold it up

explanation.surface: Glasses are raised, and someone bows to either side in acknowledgement.
explanation.definitionFit: Round-shouldered describes a posture with the shoulders hunched and curved forward on each side.

clue.text: Prior to Quins trials, dropped now and then

indicators.note: letters are dropped at regular intervals, leaving every other letter of the two words

explanation.surface: Players dropped from occasional Harlequins trials beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: Quins is the nickname of Harlequins, a London rugby club. Keep the second, fourth and so on of 'Quins trials'.
explanation.definitionFit: Until means up to the time of something, so it stands for prior to.

clue.text: Something we say is elusive or remains?

definitions.text: Something we say is elusive or remains?

parts.words: Something we say is elusive or remains?
parts.note: things scarce and hard to get are said to be like this precious powder; read literally it is the remains of gold

explanation.surface: A musing on how a precious thing either slips away or leaves traces behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'like gold dust' means very hard to get; 'remains' points to dust as leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold dust is the stock comparison for anything scarce and sought after.

clue.text: One should sit in bed to work, in the main

definitions.text: One should sit in bed to work, in the main

parts.words: One should sit in bed to work, in the main
parts.note: the bed is the seabed and the main is the open sea; this device only holds a ship when lodged on the bottom

explanation.surface: Advice that a person mostly ought to do their work sitting in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' reads as 'mostly' but means at sea; 'bed' is the seabed.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's mooring weight only works when it digs into the seabed beneath the ocean.

clue.text: Cavil at Tube-rail returns showing invalidation

indicators.note: returns says the hidden letters are read backwards
showing says the letters are on display inside the words before it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone quibbles about a London Underground rail, perhaps a complaint brought back.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave the run no indicator; 'showing' is it, displaying letters inside 'Cavil at Tube-rail', and 'returns' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal is a refutation, an argument that shows a claim to be invalid.

clue.text: Decoration sported by a boater?

parts.note: a boater is a flat straw hat, and the ribbon around its crown is its trim, not anything worn by a rower

explanation.surface: An ornament worn by someone out boating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boater' looks like a person in a boat; it is the straw hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A boater's ribbon around the crown is the classic example of this hat trimming.

clue.text: Queen perhaps given male gender?

parts.note: a queen on the board is a piece, and every piece is called a man, so the queen is styled male

explanation.surface: A question about a monarch being reclassified as a man.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen is a game piece, and pieces in that game are generically called men.
explanation.definitionFit: The queen is one of the pieces, each of which is termed a man on the board.

clue.text: Father cycled — managed to get confused

indicators.note: cycled moves the last letter of the father word round to the front

parts.note: dad is an informal word for father
to lead is to manage, so managed is led

explanation.surface: Dad went for a bike ride and somehow got muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycled' looks like riding a bike; it moves the last D of DAD to the front, giving ADD.
explanation.definitionFit: Addled means muddled or unable to think clearly.

clue.text: Seven ingredients put in simmered — he added ginger?

indicators.note: seven letters from the following words are the ingredients put into the answer

explanation.surface: A cook lists seven ingredients for a stew, then adds ginger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ginger' looks like the spice in the recipe but describes a person's hair colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger is a British nickname for someone with red hair, so the question mark flags a person.

clue.text: Remedies to host failing to accept Russian money

indicators.note: to accept is to take something in, so the money goes inside
failing says the letters break down and are rearranged

parts.note: the rouble is the currency of Russia

explanation.surface: A host fails to take payment in roubles and needs a fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' shuffles the letters of 'to host', and 'accept' opens them up to take in the Russian currency.
explanation.definitionFit: To troubleshoot is to find and fix faults, so a person troubleshoots or remedies problems.

clue.text: Funny things, boats, if a person stands on top

indicators.note: in a down answer the person word sits above the boats word

parts.note: one can mean a person, as in one must try
liners are large passenger ships

explanation.surface: Comic sight: someone standing on top of ships.
explanation.definitionFit: One-liners are short jokes, so they are amusing remarks.

clue.text: Concentrates while taking in game

indicators.note: taking in means the time word holds the game inside it

parts.note: as can mean while, as in he sang as he worked
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: Someone focuses hard while watching a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge is to condense or shorten, so it concentrates a text.

clue.text: Dragon's den by the sea?

parts.note: the dragon is the fearsome landlady of a seaside guest house, a stock comic figure

explanation.surface: A monster's lair on the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dragon' suggests a mythical beast or the TV show Dragons' Den; it means a formidable landlady.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaside lodgings run by stern landladies are a staple of British humour.

clue.text: Buzzer to get service in dump

parts.note: a fly is an insect that buzzes
a tip is money left for good service

explanation.surface: A buzzing insect gets attention at a rubbish dump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buzzer' looks like a doorbell or alarm; it is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly-tip is to dump rubbish illegally, a British term.

clue.text: I say, Cadillac should be parked by American high-flier

indicators.note: parked by places the American word next to the vehicle

parts.note: a Cadillac is an example of a car, flagged by say
US is short for American, as in US citizen

explanation.surface: A driver remarks that a Cadillac ought to be parked by a Yank.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Icarus flew too close to the sun, the archetypal overreaching aviator.

clue.text: A kiss in middle of night causes cancelling

parts.note: X is the conventional symbol for a kiss

indicators.note: middle of takes the central letter of the word night

explanation.surface: A midnight kiss leads to a break-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Axing a plan means scrapping it, so axing is cancelling.

clue.text: Rubbish set alight by crowd

indicators.note: by places the crowd word beside the alight word

parts.note: to alight is to land, as a bird alights
to crowd a space is to fill it

explanation.surface: Rubbish is set on fire by a mob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alight' reads as on fire; it is the verb meaning to touch down.
explanation.definitionFit: Landfill is waste buried in the ground, and the waste itself.

clue.text: Hide in shower

definitions.meaning: to shower with missiles, or for rain to pour

explanation.surface: Someone hides in the shower cubicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelt is both a fur skin and the verb for raining down heavily.

clue.text: Moaned, beginning to get annoyed about signs of doziness

indicators.note: beginning to takes only the first letter of the following word get
about puts the annoyed word around the sleepy letters

parts.note: riled means annoyed
ZZ is the cartoon sign of someone snoozing

explanation.surface: A sleepy person grumbled as they started to get irritated.
explanation.definitionFit: To grizzle is to whine or complain fretfully, especially of a child.

clue.text: Book Sartre edited

indicators.note: an edited text has been reworked, so the letters of the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A volume by the French philosopher, revised by an editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a volume next to Sartre; it is the police verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To book someone is police slang for charging or arresting them.

clue.text: Implies knight is joking for the listeners

indicators.note: for the listeners means the phrase is heard, not read

parts.note: a knight is addressed by the title Sir; someone joking jests

explanation.surface: A knight's jokes carry a hidden meaning for the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent 'sir jests' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To suggest something is to hint at it rather than state it, which is to imply.

clue.text: Calculates 50 per cent of 13 — drink needed!

indicators.note: 50 per cent is half, so the first half of that answer is taken

parts.note: the answer to 13 across, the word meaning confused
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Doing sums on half of thirteen leaves someone in need of a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: '13' is not a number but the answer to clue 13, whose first half is used.
explanation.definitionFit: To add up a set of figures is to total or work them out.
